facts.raw_span: asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of his forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area
no history of connective tissue disease
no history of trauma
2 long, curved-line, depressed, alopecic patches on the left side of the vertex and frontal scalp area extending to the left eyebrow
lesions measured (length × width) 7 × 2 cm and 6 × 1 cm, respectively
dermoscopic examination of the alopecic area revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
broken hairs were not seen
hair pull test was negative
histopathologic examination shows predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis
direct immunofluorescence: Positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of an arc-shaped, depressed skin groove with localized linear hair loss and the histopathologic findings of lymphocytic infiltrates and hyaline fat necrosis are consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.
The patient's symptoms of linear hair loss and hair thinning, along with the dermoscopic findings of short vellus hairs and yellow dots, are suggestive of lichen planopilaris.

The patient's presentation of a bandlike grooved alopecic lesion on the frontal scalp, along with the histopathologic findings of lymphocytic infiltrates, is consistent with frontal fibrosing alopecia.
The patient's symptoms of hair loss and the dermoscopic findings of short vellus hairs and yellow dots are also consistent with alopecia areata.
The patient's presentation of an arc-shaped, depressed skin groove, along with the histopathologic findings of lymphocytic infiltrates and hyaline fat necrosis, is also suggestive of morphea.

The patient's symptoms and histopathologic findings are also consistent with scleroderma, although the absence of systemic involvement and negative antinuclear antibody test make this diagnosis less likely.
The patient's presentation of an arc-shaped, depressed skin groove, along with the dermoscopic findings of short vellus hairs and yellow dots, is also suggestive of psoriasis.

The patient's symptoms and histopathologic findings are also consistent with dermatomyositis, although the absence of muscle weakness and negative antinuclear antibody test make this diagnosis less likely.
It explains the inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis.

rationales.F01: The presence of an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove is more typical of discoid lupus erythematosus and frontal fibrosing alopecia.
rationales.F02: Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning are common features of lichen planopilaris and frontal fibrosing alopecia.
rationales.F10: The histopathologic examination showing predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis is highly suggestive of discoid lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F11: The presence of inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis is more typical of discoid lupus erythematosus and lupus profundus.
rationales.F12: The direct immunofluorescence showing granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels is highly suggestive of discoid lupus erythematosus.
